goals.en:
- Demonstrate knowledge and understanding of key statistical concepts, including sampling techniques, variable types, and foundational principles of statistical inference.

- Apply appropriate methods for inspecting, describing, and analyzing datasets, taking into account levels of measurement, distributional characteristics, and research design.

- Critically evaluate the suitability and limitations of statistical techniques in relation to research questions and data quality.

- Interpret and draw reasoned conclusions from statistical outputs, including descriptive statistics, hypothesis tests, and linear regression models.

- Communicate findings effectively, both in written form and visual representation, including discussion of methods, data characteristics, and implications of results.

- Reflect on the research process, demonstrating awareness of the strengths and limitations of quantitative analysis within broader methodological and disciplinary contexts.-

description.en:
Statistics I introduces students to foundational concepts and techniques in statistical analysis, with a strong emphasis on understanding and interpreting real-world data. The course covers descriptive statistics, core principles of sampling and probability, and introduces methods for statistical inference.

Students learn how to critically assess datasets by exploring key concepts such as measurement levels, central tendency, variability, and data distributions. Building on these fundamentals, the course explains the logic of generalization via the central limit theorem and introduces essential inferential tools such as t-tests (including F-tests for variance equality), proportion tests, and simple linear regression. A focus is placed on the practical application of these methods using real and synthetic datasets, often supported by Excel-based analysis.

Throughout the course, students also engage with research-oriented thinking by comparing statistical results to real-world findings, designing hypothesis tests, and preparing concise data interpretations. A joint assignment with the Qualitative Methods course strengthens interdisciplinary understanding by encouraging students to contrast quantitative and qualitative approaches to a shared research theme.

Statistics I lays the groundwork for more advanced methodological work in Statistics II and supports analytical thinking in GRL courses across Economics, Psychology, Earth and Environment, and Global Health, as well as in the Living Lab and Capstone projects.

Please note that minor adjustments to the syllabus or materials may be made to improve the learning experience. All updates will be announced in class and reflected on the Brightspace course page.
